automation.title: Automation Rules
automation.description: Rules that run automatically on deals. Each rule watches one stage of one pipeline and, once a deal has stayed in it for the set number of hours, unassigns the deal so it returns to the pool.

when.pipeline: When a deal is in pipeline

automation.summary: When a deal stays in {pipeline} › {stage} for {duration}, then:

conflicts.incomplete: “{rule}” needs a stage and a stay time of at least 1 hour.
conflicts.beforeLimit: “{rule}” unassigns deals after {hours}h, before the stage “{stage}” stay limit of {limit}h — the overdue alert will never appear for that stage.
conflicts.unreachable: “{blocked}” can never run: “{by}” ({hours}h) already acts first on the same deals. Make one rule more specific with an earlier time, or deactivate one.

automation.howItWorks: Rules are checked automatically every 10 minutes. The clock starts when the deal entered the stage, or when someone last assigned it — whichever is later — so reassigning a deal gives it a fresh window. Deals that are already unassigned are skipped. Unassigning a deal also unassigns its lead, the same as any reassignment. Closed stages (Won, Competitor, Archive) can't have rules. A note counts only if it was written by the currently assigned user after that clock started; the comment written when moving a deal between stages doesn't count. Stay time counts working hours only: Fridays and Saturdays (Cairo time) are not counted, so a deal that entered a stage on Thursday morning has stayed about 24 hours by Sunday morning, not 72. The clock starts at 11:59 AM on a working day: a deal that enters before 11:59 AM starts counting at 11:59 AM (at 11:30 AM its stay time is still zero), one that enters after 5:00 PM starts the next working day at 11:59 AM, and one that enters on a Friday or Saturday starts on Sunday at 11:59 AM.
